newsitem.title: USA: Northeastern U.S. spot power mixed ahead of chill.
newsitem.headline: Northeastern U.S. spot power mixed ahead of chill.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. finished mixed Friday ahead of a cold front forecast to move into the region earlier next week.

Although spot power in the Northeast failed to follow the record jump in natural gas prices this week, a lengthy cold spell could force utilities to switch on expensive oil or natgas generation to meet daily peak demand, marketers said.
"It has not happened yet, but it could push prices up to $45.00," a New York trader said.

At utility receipt points in the New York City area, swing gas values were talked as high as $5.00 per million British thermal units, compared with late Thursday's quote near $4.30. December New York City gate deliveries were discussed in the $5.00-$5.20 range.
There has been sufficient supply of coal, nuclear and hydro generation to meet current demand, he added.
In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity prices for Monday were notationally valued near $24.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from Thursday's $21.00.

Western New York prices for Monday were pegged higher in tandem with stronger values in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool. Western New York generators had been selling power into northern PJM because of more attractive prices.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Monday remained in the $14.00-$15.00 range.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity was assessed for Saturday near $20.00, Sunday $19.00 and Monday $27.00-$28.00, compared with Thursday's $26.00-$28.00.
Off-peak, non-firm power in eastern NYPP was talked for Saturday near $15.00, Sunday $14.00 and Monday $17.00-$18.00, compared with Thursday's range also at $17.00-$18.00.

In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Monday at the Northeast Utilities border was quoted at $31.00-$32.00, lower than Thursday's notational assessment of $32.00-$33.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Monday delivery to the NU border was near $21.00, flat from Thursday.
A 355 megawatt (MW) unit at the coal-fired Merrimack generating station in central New Hampshire was expected to resume operation this weekend after being shut October 25 for boiler maintenance.
